docs.text: HardFOC driver ADS7952 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Texas Instruments ADS7952 12-channel, 12-bit, 1 MSPS SAR ADC. It reads one channel or a whole sequence, programs per-channel alarms and the four GPIOs, and converts counts to volts, on any MCU with SPI. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes over SPI; it does the rest: the 16-bit command words, the two-frame result pipeline, the power-up discard, sequence and alarm programming and the conversion to volts. 12-channel, 12-bit, 1 MSPS SAR ADC ADS7952 Texas Instruments Inputs 12 single-ended channels through one multiplexer (MXO, wired to AINP) Interface SPI mode 0 up to 20 MHz, 16-bit frames, MSB first Input range 0 to VREF, or 0 to 2 × VREF while 2 × VREF ≤ +VA; external VREF 2.0 V to 3.0 V Supply +VA 2.7 V to 5.25 V (analog), +VBD 1.7 V to +VA (digital I/O) Extras Manual, Auto-1 and Auto-2 sequencing; high and low alarm per channel; 4 GPIOs (TSSOP) Package 38-pin TSSOP (DBT) or 32-pin VQFN (RHB, one GPIO); −40 °C to 125 °C Datasheet (SLAS605C) · Product page What you get ¶ One object per chip. ADS7952<YourSpi> reads channels, switches modes and programs sequences, alarms and GPIOs. See API guide . Results matched to their channel. Every reply carries the 4-bit address of the channel it belongs to; the driver keys on it instead of counting frames. See Modes and the frame pipeline . Volts in and out. Counts convert with the reference and range you run, and alarm thresholds take volts. See Configuration . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class with one method: no virtual calls, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, configure, read, program alarms and GPIOs, and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Adc standing for ads7952::ADS7952<MySpi> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One ADS7952<SpiType> object per chip. It owns no hardware: it holds a reference to your port and mirrors what it has programmed into the chip. Group Calls Returns Initialise EnsureInitialized(force) , IsInitialized() bool Read ReadChannel(ch) , ReadAllChannels() , RawManualFrames(ch, out, n) ReadResult , ChannelReadings , frame count Modes EnterManualMode(ch) , EnterAuto1Mode(reset) , EnterAuto2Mode(reset) , GetMode() bool Sequences ProgramAuto1Channels(mask) , ProgramAuto2LastChannel(ch) bool Alarms and GPIOs ProgramAlarm() , ProgramAlarmVoltage() , ProgramGPIO(config) , SetGPIOOutputs(bits) bool ( void for outputs) Range and power SetRange(range) , SetPowerDown(pd) bool Conversion CountToVoltage() , VoltageToCount() , SetVref() , SetVA() , GetActiveVref() volts, counts Reads return a struct with an error field and an ok() helper. The other calls return false only for an argument out of range (a channel above 11): the SPI port returns nothing, so the driver cannot see a bus failure there. Initialise ¶ #include "ads7952.hpp" #include <cstdio> int read_adc ( MySpi & spi ) { ads7952 :: ADS7952 < MySpi > adc ( spi , 2.5f , 5.0f ); // REFP = 2.5 V, +VA = 5 V if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. discard power-up frame, program sequences return -1 ; } const ads7952 :: ReadResult ch3 = adc . ReadChannel ( 3 ); // 2. one channel (Manual mode) if ( ! ch3 . ok ()) { return -1 ; // Timeout: wiring, SPI mode or CS framing } std :: printf ( "CH3 = %.3f V (%u counts) 
 " , ch3 . voltage , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch3 . count )); const ads7952 :: ChannelReadings all = adc . ReadAllChannels (); // 3. every channel (Auto-1 mode) for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < 12 ; ++ ch ) { if ( all . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "CH%u = %.3f V 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch ), all . voltage [ ch ]); } } return all . ok () ? 0 : -1 ; } EnsureInitialized() discards the invalid first conversion, programs the Auto-1 mask and the Auto-2 last channel from ADS7952_CFG and enters Auto-1. A second call returns true without SPI traffic; pass force = true after the chip was reset or lost power. Every read returns Error::NotInitialized until it has succeeded. Configure ¶ // Auto-1 scans any subset; Auto-2 scans CH0..last. Program them once after EnsureInitialized(). if ( ! adc . ProgramAuto1Channels ( ads7952 :: ChannelMask ( 0 , 1 , 4 , 5 ))) { return false ; } if ( ! adc . ProgramAuto2LastChannel ( 7 )) { // CH0..CH7 return false ; } // 0..2 x VREF: only valid while 2 x VREF <= +VA (2.5 V reference, 5 V supply). adc . SetRange ( ads7952 :: Range :: TwoVref ); if ( ! adc . EnterAuto1Mode ()) { // a mode frame latches the range bit on the chip return false ; } Build masks with ads7952::ChannelMask(0, 2, 4) , ChannelRangeMask(first, last) or the constants kAllChannels , kEvenChannels , kOddChannels , kFirstFour , kSecondFour , kThirdFour . Bit N is channel N. SetRange() changes the driver's full scale at once, but the chip applies the new range only with the next mode frame, hence the EnterAuto1Mode() after it. Modes and the frame pipeline explains which calls send one. Read ¶ // One channel: Manual mode, three frames, keyed on the channel address in the reply. const ads7952 :: ReadResult r = adc . ReadChannel ( 4 ); if ( r . ok ()) { std :: printf ( "CH%u: %u counts, %.3f V 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( r . channel ), static_cast < unsigned > ( r . count ), r . voltage ); } // Every channel of the Auto-1 mask: one frame per channel plus two. const ads7952 :: ChannelReadings all = adc . ReadAllChannels (); for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < ads7952 :: ChannelReadings :: MAX_CHANNELS ; ++ ch ) { if ( all . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "CH%u: %.3f V 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch ), all . voltage [ ch ]); } } if ( ! all . ok ()) { std :: printf ( "%u of the programmed channels arrived 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( all . validChannelCount ())); } Call Frames (healthy) Frames (most) Leaves the chip in ReadChannel(ch) 3 1 + MANUAL_READ_MAX_FRAMES Manual, on ch ReadAllChannels() N + 2 1 + N + READ_ALL_MAX_EXTRA_FRAMES Auto-1 N is the number of channels in the Auto-1 mask. ReadAllChannels() always uses the Auto-1 mask. ChannelReadings::valid_mask says which entries of count[] and voltage[] were filled; on Error::Timeout the channels that did arrive are still valid. Program alarms and GPIOs ¶ // GPIO0 goes high while any channel is outside its window (active-high output). ads7952 :: GPIOConfig gpio ; gpio . alarm_mode = ads7952 :: GPIO01AlarmMode :: GPIO0_HighAndLowAlarm ; gpio . direction_mask = ads7952 :: gpio :: kGPIO2 | ads7952 :: gpio :: kGPIO3 ; // GPIO2, GPIO3: outputs if ( ! adc . ProgramGPIO ( gpio )) { return false ; } // A window of 0.5 V .. 2.0 V on CH0, from volts with the active reference ... if ( ! adc . ProgramAlarmVoltage ( 0 , ads7952 :: AlarmBound :: Low , 0.5f ) || ! adc . ProgramAlarmVoltage ( 0 , ads7952 :: AlarmBound :: High , 2.0f )) { return false ; } // ... or from counts. The chip keeps the top 10 bits (4-count steps). if ( ! adc . ProgramAlarm ( 1 , ads7952 :: AlarmBound :: High , 3000 )) { return false ; } Each channel has a high and a low threshold. The chip compares the top 10 bits of each conversion with them, so a threshold has a resolution of 4 counts. ProgramAlarmVoltage() converts with the reference that is active when you call it: program the thresholds again after SetRange() or SetVref() . GPIO01AlarmMode DI06:04 GPIO0 GPIO1 GPIO 000 GPIO GPIO GPIO0_HighAndLowAlarm 001 High or low alarm GPIO GPIO0_HighAlarm 010 High alarm GPIO GPIO1_HighAlarm 100 GPIO Low alarm (the datasheet's function for this code) GPIO1_LowAlarm_GPIO0_HighAlarm 110 High alarm Low alarm GPIOConfig::gpio2_as_range_input and gpio3_as_powerdown_input hand the range and power-down control to those pins; reset_all_registers resets every chip register in the next frame. On the VQFN package only GPIO0 exists. Write outputs and power down ¶ // GPIO outputs and power-down ride in every mode frame; a mode frame latches them. adc . SetGPIOOutputs ( ads7952 :: gpio :: kGPIO2 ); // GPIO2 high, GPIO3 low adc . SetPowerDown ( ads7952 :: PowerDown :: PowerDown ); if ( ! adc . EnterAuto1Mode ()) { // latched here: the chip powers down return false ; } adc . SetPowerDown ( ads7952 :: PowerDown :: Normal ); if ( ! adc . EnterAuto1Mode ()) { // awake again return false ; } The power-down and GPIO bits travel in every mode frame, like the range. In power-down the chip draws about 1 µA; the next mode frame with the bit cleared wakes it, and it is ready after 1 µs. Read raw frames ¶ // Bring-up: clock frames by hand and see the address pipeline (CH in DO15:12, count in DO11:0). uint16_t words [ 4 ] = {}; const uint8_t n = adc . RawManualFrames ( 6 , words , 4 ); for ( uint8_t i = 0 ; i < n ; ++ i ) { std :: printf ( "frame %u: CH%u = %u 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( i ), static_cast < unsigned > ( words [ i ] >> 12 ), static_cast < unsigned > ( words [ i ] & 0x0FFF )); } RawManualFrames() sends one Manual frame and n - 1 continue frames and returns every reply untouched. Use it on the bench to see the address pipeline advance; it leaves the chip in Manual mode. Handle errors ¶ const ads7952 :: ReadResult r = adc . ReadChannel ( 2 ); switch ( r . error ) { case ads7952 :: Error :: Ok : break ; case ads7952 :: Error :: NotInitialized : // call EnsureInitialized() first adc . EnsureInitialized (); break ; case ads7952 :: Error :: InvalidChannel : // channel > 11 break ; case ads7952 :: Error :: Timeout : // the address never came back: check the bus adc . EnsureInitialized ( true ); // after a reset or brown-out, program again break ; default : break ; } Signal Meaning What to do Error::NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded Call it Error::InvalidChannel Channel above 11 Fix the caller Error::Timeout The requested channel address never came back in the frame budget Check SPI mode, CS framing and MISO; re-initialise after a chip reset A bool call returns false Channel or last channel above 11 Fix the caller Error::SpiError , ProgrammingFailed and ModeChangeFailed exist in the enum but no call returns them today. SetVref ( measured_vref ); // e.g. 2.497 V measured at REFP const float v = adc . CountToVoltage ( 2048 ); // with the active reference (range applied) const uint16_t c = ads7952 :: VoltageToCount ( 1.25f , adc . GetActiveVref ()); std :: printf ( "2048 counts = %.4f V, 1.25 V = %u counts 
 " , v , static_cast < unsigned > ( c )); SetVref() and SetVA() only change the numbers the driver converts with; they send nothing. Measure REFP once on your board and pass the real value for the best absolute accuracy. Configuration covers the limits these values are clamped to.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS7952 object, whose public calls (listed from inc/ads7952.hpp) read channels, switch modes and program sequences, alarms and GPIOs. The core builds the 16-bit command words, keys every result on the channel address in DO15:12 and converts counts to volts. It reaches the bus through the CRTP SpiInterface (inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp), whose one method the platform port implements: a full-duplex transfer with chip select held low. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads7952.hpp ADS7952 public calls ; inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where Depends on You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : ADS7952<SpiType> inc/ads7952.hpp , src/ads7952.ipp The port's transfer() Never, for a new board SPI interface : SpiInterface<Derived> inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp The port's transfer() Never Platform port : your class Your project Your SDK Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as ADS7952 core participant P as Your port participant C as ADS7952 chip A->>D: ReadChannel(3) D->>D: check initialised, channel < 12 D->>P: transfer(MANUAL | CH3 | range, power, GPIO bits) P->>C: 16 clocks, CS low C-->>D: stale reply (discarded) loop until DO15:12 == 3, at most MANUAL_READ_MAX_FRAMES D->>P: transfer(CONTINUE) P->>C: 16 clocks, CS low C-->>D: DO15:12 channel, DO11:0 count end D->>D: count to volts with the active reference D-->>A: ReadResult{count, voltage, channel, error} Design choices ¶ CRTP, not a virtual base. The port is a template parameter, so the compiler calls transfer() directly and can inline it; there is no vtable and no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: ADS7952<MySpi> . No heap, no exceptions. The driver holds a reference to your port and a few bytes of state (mode, range, masks, reference voltages). Every call is noexcept . Synchronous and imperative. Each call sends its frames and returns; there is no state machine or background task. The driver is not thread-safe: give each chip one owner, or guard calls with a mutex. Address-keyed results. The chip tags every reply with its channel, so the driver matches on the tag instead of trusting a frame count ( Modes and the frame pipeline ). State mirrored in software. The chip has no readable registers. The driver remembers what it programmed ( GetMode() , GetRange() , GetAuto1ChannelMask() , GetAuto2LastChannel() ); after a chip reset or brown-out, call EnsureInitialized(true) to program it again. docs.text: CRTP, not a virtual base. The port is a template parameter, so the compiler calls transfer() directly and can inline it; there is no vtable and no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: ADS7952<MySpi> . No heap, no exceptions. The driver holds a reference to your port and a few bytes of state (mode, range, masks, reference voltages). Every call is noexcept . Synchronous and imperative. Each call sends its frames and returns; there is no state machine or background task. The driver is not thread-safe: give each chip one owner, or guard calls with a mutex. Address-keyed results. The chip tags every reply with its channel, so the driver matches on the tag instead of trusting a frame count ( Modes and the frame pipeline ). State mirrored in software. The chip has no readable registers. The driver remembers what it programmed ( GetMode() , GetRange() , GetAuto1ChannelMask() , GetAuto2LastChannel() ); after a chip reset or brown-out, call EnsureInitialized(true) to program it again.

ProgramGPIO() can give three of them a fixed function; the outputs are active high. Pin Name Alternative function 37 GPIO0 High alarm, or combined high-or-low alarm output 38 GPIO1 Low alarm output 1 GPIO2 Range input: high selects 0 to 2 × VREF, low 0 to VREF 2 GPIO3 Power-down input, active low Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Mode SPI mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first Speed Up to 20 MHz (f SCLK , any +VBD); the ESP32 examples use 4 MHz Frame 16 bits: command DI15:0 in, reply DO15:0 out, full duplex Chip select Low for exactly one frame, then high for at least t w1 = 20 ns Reply DO15:12 channel address (or GPIO input levels), DO11:0 the 12-bit count Latency A channel selected in frame N is converted in frame N + 2 The driver sends every frame as one two-byte transfer() , so your port only has to keep CS low across both bytes and release it afterwards. Modes and the frame pipeline explains the latency and how the driver deals with it. Timing ¶ Minimums and maximums from the timing requirements (Section 7.9, 50 pF load), at the three I/O supply ranges. Short them on the board (TI's reference design does), or put your buffer or filter between them. Source impedance. Decouple REFP with 10 µF next to the pin (the datasheet's application circuit uses a REF5025). Ground the NC pins (11 to 14 on the TSSOP).

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every driver call is noexcept and returns bool or a result struct. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ads7952-driver.git external/hf-ads7952-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-ads7952-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-ads7952-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::ads7952 ) # or hf_ads7952 The hf_ads7952 target (alias hf::ads7952 ) is an INTERFACE library. It carries the include directories ( inc/ , src/ and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_ADS7952_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF Adds -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic to targets that link the driver HF_ADS7952_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) cmake --install installs the headers and a package configuration, so an installed copy is found with find_package(hf_ads7952 CONFIG REQUIRED) and linked as hf::ads7952 . ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_ads7952/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_ADS7952_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_ads7952 . The driver class also reports it: ADS7952<MySpi>::GetDriverVersionMajor() , GetDriverVersionMinor() and GetDriverVersionPatch() . Compile-time switches ¶ The defaults in inc/ads7952_config.hpp can be overridden with CONFIG_ADS7952_* defines: reference and supply voltage, the power-up Auto-1 mask and Auto-2 last channel, the default range and the frame budgets of the read loops. docs.text: Modes and the frame pipeline ¶ How the ADS7952 picks channels, why a result arrives two frames after its command, and which settings need a mode frame before the chip applies them. Three channel modes ¶ Mode Channels Driver calls Use it for Manual The one the host names in each frame ReadChannel() , EnterManualMode() , RawManualFrames() Reading a channel on demand Auto-1 Any subset, in ascending order, from a 12-bit mask ProgramAuto1Channels() , EnterAuto1Mode() , ReadAllChannels() Scanning a fixed set of channels Auto-2 CH0 up to a programmed last channel ProgramAuto2LastChannel() , EnterAuto2Mode() Scanning a contiguous block EnsureInitialized() programs the Auto-1 mask ( ADS7952_CFG::DEFAULT_AUTO1_MASK , all 12 channels) and the Auto-2 last channel ( DEFAULT_AUTO2_LAST_CH , CH11) and leaves the chip in Auto-1. ReadChannel() moves it to Manual; ReadAllChannels() moves it back to Auto-1 and restarts the sequence. The command word ¶ Every frame carries one 16-bit command on SDI. In Manual, Auto-1 and Auto-2 it is the mode control register: Bits Field Meaning DI15:12 Mode 0001 Manual, 0010 Auto-1, 0011 Auto-2, 0000 continue in the current mode DI11 Program 1: apply DI06:00 in this frame (Auto-1, Auto-2: DI10:00); 0: keep the previous values DI10 Reset counter (Auto) 1: restart the sequence at its first channel DI10:07 Channel (Manual) Channel to select next, applied whatever DI11 says DI06 Range 0: 0 to VREF; 1: 0 to 2 × VREF DI05 Power down 1: power down at the 16 th SCLK falling edge DI04 Output select 0: DO15:12 carries the channel address; 1: the GPIO input levels DI03:00 GPIO data Levels of the GPIOs configured as outputs Other values of DI15:12 open the program registers: 0100 GPIO, 1000 and 1001 the Auto-1 mask and Auto-2 last channel, 1100 to 1110 the alarm thresholds of channels 0-3, 4-7 and 8-11. The constants are in inc/ads7952_registers.hpp ; the driver keeps DI04 at 0 so every reply is tagged. The reply word and its latency ¶ The reply on SDO is the conversion of the input sampled at this frame's CS falling edge: Bits Field DO15:12 Channel address of the conversion (DI04 = 0) DO11:00 12-bit count, MSB first A channel named in frame N is selected at the end of frame N, acquired during frame N + 1 and sampled at the start of frame N + 2. Its result therefore comes back in frame N + 2, and the replies in frames N and N + 1 belong to channels chosen earlier. The driver never relies on counting frames. ReadChannel() sends the Manual frame, then clocks continue frames until DO15:12 equals the channel it asked for (at most ADS7952_CFG::MANUAL_READ_MAX_FRAMES , default 4), and returns Error::Timeout if it never does. ReadAllChannels() restarts Auto-1 and keeps each reply whose address is in the mask, until every programmed channel has arrived or the budget (one frame per channel plus READ_ALL_MAX_EXTRA_FRAMES , default 4) runs out. Settings that need a mode frame ¶ A continue frame (DI15:12 = 0000 ) keeps the mode, and the chip ignores DI11:00 in it (datasheet Table 7). SetRange() , SetPowerDown() and SetGPIOOutputs() update the driver's state and send a continue frame, so the chip applies the new range, power-down or GPIO levels only with the next frame that has DI11 = 1: Call Sends DI11 = 1 Applies a pending range, power-down or GPIO change EnterManualMode() , EnterAuto1Mode() , EnterAuto2Mode() yes yes ReadAllChannels() yes yes ReadChannel() , RawManualFrames() no no SetRange() , SetPowerDown() , SetGPIOOutputs() no no Call one of the Enter...Mode() functions after changing these settings, as the API guide does. CountToVoltage() switches to the new reference at once, so until the chip has latched the range, counts are converted with the wrong full scale. Programming sequences ¶ Register Frames Driver call Auto-1 mask 2: 1000 , then the mask in DI11:00 ProgramAuto1Channels(mask) Auto-2 last channel 1: 1001 with the channel in DI09:06 ProgramAuto2LastChannel(ch) GPIO configuration 1: 0100 with the functions and directions ProgramGPIO(config) One alarm threshold 3: group, threshold with the exit bit, one continue frame ProgramAlarm() , ProgramAlarmVoltage() The chip keeps converting in its current mode while it is being programmed, and the replies stay valid; the driver discards them. docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the SPI interface, with one method. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls transfer() on a class you derive from ads7952::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the call is resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS7952 object, whose public calls (listed from inc/ads7952.hpp) read channels, switch modes and program sequences, alarms and GPIOs. The core builds the 16-bit command words, keys every result on the channel address in DO15:12 and converts counts to volts. It reaches the bus through the CRTP SpiInterface (inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp), whose one method the platform port implements: a full-duplex transfer with chip select held low. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads7952.hpp ADS7952 public calls ; inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract void transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) Assert CS, clock len bytes out of tx while reading len bytes into rx , release CS. The driver always passes len = 2 and both buffers There is nothing else: no GPIOs, no delays, no logging. The chip has no reset or data-ready pin, and its timing is set by SCLK and CS. The port ¶ my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public ads7952 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // One 16-bit frame: SPI mode 0, MSB first, CS low for both bytes and high again afterwards. void transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 0 , MSB first, at most 20 MHz. One frame per call. CS goes low before the first clock and high after the 16 th ; never split the two bytes into separate CS cycles, never merge two calls into one. The chip samples its input on the CS falling edge. CS high for at least 20 ns between frames (t w1 ). Most SPI peripherals give far more. Byte order as given. tx[0] is DI15:8 and goes first; rx[0] receives DO15:8. transfer() returns void , so a port cannot report a bus failure to the driver. Log it in the port; the driver sees the garbage reply and ReadChannel() returns Error::Timeout when the channel address does not come back. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_ads7952_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF spi_master device in mode 0 with hardware CS, one spi_device_transmit() per frame. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/my_spi.hpp , with the driver instantiated over it. Call EnsureInitialized() , then RawManualFrames(5, words, 4) : words[2] >> 12 must be 5. If the address never matches, look at the bus with a logic analyser (mode, CS framing, byte order). Put a known voltage on one input and compare ReadChannel() with a meter. Use the measured REFP with SetVref() . Read two channels with very different voltages in turn: if the second reads close to the first, the source impedance is too high for your SCLK rate ( Hardware ). Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each ADS7952 one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. If the SPI bus is shared, your SDK's bus lock must cover a whole transfer() call.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Read the ADS7952 from your MCU: wire the SPI bus and the analog front end, write a one-method port class, call three driver functions. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU ADS7952 (TSSOP-38 pin) Notes SPI SCLK SCLK (32) SPI mode 0, up to 20 MHz; start at 1 MHz to 4 MHz SPI MOSI SDI (33) 16-bit command word, MSB first SPI MISO SDO (34) 16-bit reply: channel address in DO15:12, count in DO11:0 SPI CS CS (31) Active low; one CS frame per 16-bit word I/O supply +VBD (36), BDGND (35) 1.7 V to +VA; sets the logic levels, so match your MCU GND AGND, BDGND Common ground On the analog side, connect MXO (7) to AINP (8) and AINM (9) to AGND: the multiplexer output is not routed to the converter inside the chip. Put a 2.0 V to 3.0 V reference on REFP (4) with REFM (3) to AGND, and +VA (5, 29) at 2.7 V to 5.25 V. The Hardware page has every pin, the bus timing and the power ranges. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf_ads7952 CMake target (or add inc/ and src/ to your include path and build with C++20). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ads7952-driver.git external/hf-ads7952-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: one full-duplex transfer with chip select held low for the whole word. Replace platform_spi_transfer() with your SDK's call. my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public ads7952 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // One 16-bit frame: SPI mode 0, MSB first, CS low for both bytes and high again afterwards. void transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } }; The driver always calls transfer() with two bytes. Porting explains the contract and shows how to check a port. 4. Read the channels ¶ main.cpp #include "ads7952.hpp" #include <cstdio> int read_adc ( MySpi & spi ) { ads7952 :: ADS7952 < MySpi > adc ( spi , 2.5f , 5.0f ); // REFP = 2.5 V, +VA = 5 V if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. discard power-up frame, program sequences return -1 ; } const ads7952 :: ReadResult ch3 = adc . ReadChannel ( 3 ); // 2. one channel (Manual mode) if ( ! ch3 . ok ()) { return -1 ; // Timeout: wiring, SPI mode or CS framing } std :: printf ( "CH3 = %.3f V (%u counts) \n " , ch3 . voltage , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch3 . count )); const ads7952 :: ChannelReadings all = adc . ReadAllChannels (); // 3. every channel (Auto-1 mode) for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < 12 ; ++ ch ) { if ( all . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "CH%u = %.3f V \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch ), all . voltage [ ch ]); } } return all . ok () ? 0 : -1 ; } What each step does: The constructor stores the reference (REFP) and supply (+VA) voltages used to convert counts to volts. It sends nothing. EnsureInitialized() discards the invalid first conversion after power-up, programs the Auto-1 sequence (all 12 channels) and the Auto-2 last channel (CH11), and enters Auto-1 mode. Calling it again does nothing. ReadChannel() selects one channel in Manual mode and clocks frames until the reply carries that channel's address: three frames when the bus is healthy. ReadAllChannels() restarts the Auto-1 sequence and collects one result per programmed channel. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check ReadChannel() returns Error::Timeout SPI mode 0, CS low for all 16 clocks and high between words, MISO wiring Every count is 0 +VA and the reference are present; MXO is connected to AINP Every count is 4095 The input is above the range: VREF, or 2 × VREF in Range::TwoVref Every channel reads the same count MXO to AINP wiring, source impedance; see Troubleshooting Next ¶ API guide : sequences, ranges, alarms, GPIOs and errors. ReadChannel ( 3 ); // 2. one channel (Manual mode) if ( ! ch3 . ok ()) { return -1 ; // Timeout: wiring, SPI mode or CS framing } std :: printf ( "CH3 = %.3f V (%u counts) \n " , ch3 . voltage , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch3 . count )); const ads7952 :: ChannelReadings all = adc . ReadAllChannels (); // 3. every channel (Auto-1 mode) for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < 12 ; ++ ch ) { if ( all . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "CH%u = %.3f V \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( ch ), all . voltage [ ch ]); } } return all . ok () ? 0 : -1 ; } What each step does: The constructor stores the reference (REFP) and supply (+VA) voltages used to convert counts to volts. It sends nothing. EnsureInitialized() discards the invalid first conversion after power-up, programs the Auto-1 sequence (all 12 channels) and the Auto-2 last channel (CH11), and enters Auto-1 mode. Calling it again does nothing. ReadChannel() selects one channel in Manual mode and clocks frames until the reply carries that channel's address: three frames when the bus is healthy. ReadAllChannels() restarts the Auto-1 sequence and collects one result per programmed channel. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests against a model of the chip, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an ADS7952, their causes and the fix for each. Start with RawManualFrames() : it shows the raw replies, so it tells bus problems (no address, wrong address) apart from analog problems (right address, wrong count). API guide shows the call. Bus and protocol ¶ Symptom Cause Fix ReadChannel() returns Error::Timeout on every channel The reply address never matches: wrong SPI mode, CS released between the two bytes, MISO not connected SPI mode 0; one CS cycle per 2-byte transfer() ; check SDO with a logic analyser Every reply is 0x0000 or 0xFFFF No supply on +VBD, MISO floating, or CS never goes low Measure +VBD (1.7 V to +VA); check CS on the scope Addresses look right but shifted by one frame Your port splits or merges frames, so the chip and the driver count frames differently Exactly 16 clocks per CS low ReadAllChannels() returns Error::Timeout with some channels missing Auto-1 mask on the chip differs from the driver's (chip reset or brown-out since EnsureInitialized() ) EnsureInitialized(true) after any reset; check valid_mask Every read returns Error::NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() was never called on this object Call it once after power-up Readings ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Every count is 0 MXO not connected to AINP, AINP floating, or no reference Short MXO (pin 7) to AINP (pin 8); AINM to AGND; check REFP Counts stuck at 4095 Input above the range Use Range::TwoVref (needs 2 × VREF ≤ +VA) or scale the input Every channel reads about the same count Source impedance too high: the sampling capacitor keeps the previous channel's charge 50 Ω or less into each input, or about 150 pF at each input; or lower SCLK Voltages off by a fixed factor vref passed to the driver is not the voltage at REFP, or it was clamped (above 2.5 V) Measure REFP; SetVref() ; see Configuration Voltages off by exactly 2 after SetRange() The chip has not latched the new range yet: SetRange() sends a continue frame, which the chip ignores Call EnterAuto1Mode() (or another Enter...Mode() ) after SetRange() The first conversion after power-up is wrong The chip's first conversion is invalid by design EnsureInitialized() discards it; after a reset call EnsureInitialized(true) Alarms and GPIOs ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Alarm pin never changes GPIO0/GPIO1 not assigned an alarm function ProgramGPIO() with a GPIO01AlarmMode other than GPIO Alarm fires at the wrong voltage after a range change Thresholds are stored as counts Call ProgramAlarmVoltage() again after SetRange() or SetVref() GPIO1_HighAlarm gives a low alarm That code (DI06:04 = 100 ) is the datasheet's GPIO1 low-alarm setting Use it as a low alarm; see API guide GPIO outputs do not change GPIO not configured as output, or no mode frame since SetGPIOOutputs() Set the bit in direction_mask ; call an Enter...Mode() after SetGPIOOutputs() Only GPIO0 responds VQFN package: GPIO1 to GPIO3 do not exist Use the TSSOP package for four GPIOs Build ¶ Symptom Cause Fix 'ads7952.ipp' file not found src/ is not on the include path Link the hf_ads7952 target, or add both inc/ and src/ hf::ads7952 not found add_subdirectory() missing, or find_package(hf_ads7952 CONFIG) without an install See Installation Errors about C++20 Compiler older than GCC 10 / Clang 12, or the standard forced lower The target requires cxx_std_20 ; do not override it

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Three layers, one of them yours ¶ Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS7952 object, whose public calls (listed from inc/ads7952.hpp) read channels, switch modes and program sequences, alarms and GPIOs. The core builds the 16-bit command words, keys every result on the channel address in DO15:12 and converts counts to volts. It reaches the bus through the CRTP SpiInterface (inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp), whose one method the platform port implements: a full-duplex transfer with chip select held low.
